newsitem.title: USA: White House drug chief sees rise in chemical drugs.
newsitem.headline: White House drug chief sees rise in chemical drugs.

text.p: Strict law enforcement will never stop the use of illegal drugs but it could help stem the spread of more dangerous drugs manufactured from chemicals, the nation's top drug fighter told a national gathering of sheriffs on Monday.

"Law enforcement cannot solve the problem of drug abuse in America," Barry McCaffrey, director of the president's Office of National Drug Control Policy, told a meeting of the National Sheriff's Association.

McCaffrey said it may be necessary to require anyone arrested to submit to rehabilitation if they test positive for drugs. "In New York City, 83 percent of the people busted test positive for an illegal drug," he said.

"The American people think you're going to solve the problem of drug abuse and I don't think you can," he told the sheriffs. "I think it's going to be parents and ministers and coaches and schoolteachers and community coalitions."
The government estimates that 12 million Americans regularly use illegal drugs and 3.6 million are addicted, including 600,000 addicted to heroin.
McCaffrey warned that chemically engineered "boutique" drugs such as methamphetamine pose a greater problem for law enforcement officers because they do not have to be smuggled into the country.
"In 15 years, that will probably be the principal drug threat to American law enforcement and prison systems. It is going to be a nightmare if we don't get organised and confront it," he said.

"You should wish you're going to pull over a nice, dozing off heroin addict, as opposed to somebody who has been awake for three to 15 days and whose personality is now unravelling, they're tweaking with paranoid behaviour, because they're addicted to methamphetamine and they're afraid to come off the high," McCaffrey said.
He also said makeshift laboratories used to manufacture illegal drugs leave dangerous chemical residues and can cost $35,000 to clean up.
